title: A two-sided inequality for the zeta function, digamma function, and cotangent
statement:
Let $B_1(x)$ be the first Bernoulli polynomial, let $\psi$ denote the digamma function, and let $\gamma=-\psi(1)$ be the Euler–Mascheroni constant. Define

$$
\overline{b}:=\overline{B_1(\gamma)}=\gamma+\frac{1}{2},\qquad b:=B_1(\gamma)=\gamma-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

For $0<x<1$, **the inequality conjecture.**

$$
\pi\cot(\pi x)+x<\zeta(x)-\psi(x)<\pi\cot(\pi x)+\overline{b}x+b.
$$

This inequality would give a simple comparison between the Euler–Riemann zeta function, the digamma function, and the cotangent on the unit interval. The source presents it as a problem arising from the study of a related theorem; no resolution is supplied here.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.00631

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2026).
source_name: Michael Andrew Henry, “A simple inequality relating the Euler-Riemann zeta function, digamma, and cotangent over the unit interval”, arXiv:2601.00631 (2026).
